name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q143 - Germ layer origin of mammalian amnion

questiontext.text: The amnion of mammalian embryo is derived from

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Mammalian embryos develop extraembryonic membranes (amnion, chorion, allantois, yolk sac) to protect, nourish, and accommodate the developing fetus.

Evaluation of Concepts: The amnion is a double-layered membrane formed by an inner layer of ectoderm and an outer layer of somatic mesoderm (somatopleure). It encloses the amniotic cavity filled with amniotic fluid, which cushions the embryo against mechanical shocks.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the amnion is derived from ectoderm and mesoderm.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q144 - Placental hormones maintaining pregnancy

questiontext.text: Hormones secreted by the placenta to maintain pregnancy are

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine gland during pregnancy, secreting hormones necessary for maintaining the uterine lining, supporting fetal growth, and preparing maternal tissues.

Evaluation of Concepts: Hormones produced and secreted by the placenta include human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), progestogens (progesterone), and estrogens. Relaxin is primarily produced by the corpus luteum (and later in small amounts by placenta), while oxytocin and prolactin are secreted by the pituitary gland, and glucocorticoids by adrenal glands.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, hormones secreted by the placenta to maintain pregnancy are hCG, hPL, progestogens, and estrogens.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q145 - Distinguishing spermiogenesis from spermiation

  • Spermiation: The final release of mature spermatozoa from the protective Sertoli cells into the lumen of the seminiferous tubules.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q147 - Distinguishing features of ciliates among protozoans

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q148 - Vertebrate group characterized by crop and gizzard

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q149 - Sexual dimorphism features in male cockroach

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q150 - Identification of non homeothermic animal

questiontext.text: Which one of these animals is not a homeotherm ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Animals are classified thermo-physiologically as homeotherms (warm-blooded organisms that maintain a constant body temperature) or poikilotherms (cold-blooded organisms whose body temperature fluctuates with environmental temperature).

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q151 - Identification of animal lacking metamorphosis stage

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Moths undergo complete metamorphosis (egg \(\rightarrow\) larva/caterpillar \(\rightarrow\) pupa \(\rightarrow\) adult).
  • Tunicates undergo retrogressive metamorphosis from a motile tadpole larva to a sessile adult.
  • Starfish undergo metamorphosis from a free-swimming larva (bipinnaria/brachiolaria) into a radial adult.
  • Earthworms exhibit direct development without any larval stage or metamorphosis; juvenile hatchlings resemble miniature adults.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, earthworms do not undergo metamorphosis.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q152 - Chief primary producers in marine ocean ecosystems

questiontext.text: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Aquatic ecosystems rely on photosynthetic planktonic organisms as primary producers at the base of the food web.

Evaluation of Concepts: Diatoms (Chrysophytes) are microscopic single-celled algae with silica-reinforced cell walls (frustules). They contribute a massive fraction of global carbon fixation and are recognized as the primary/chief producers in marine ocean ecosystems.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, diatoms are known as the chief producers in the oceans.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q153 - Population interaction used in antibiotic production

questiontext.text: Which one of the following population interactions is widely used in medical science for the production of antibiotics ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Population interactions describe biotic relationships where one species affects another negatively, positively, or neutrally.

Evaluation of Concepts: Amensalism is an interaction in which one organism inhibits or harms another organism without being affected or harmed itself. Production of antibiotics (such as penicillin by the fungus Penicillium notatum) inhibits bacterial growth without providing direct metabolic benefit or harm to the mold, representing amensalism.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, amensalism is the population interaction widely used in medical science for antibiotic production.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q154 - Identification of non ex situ conservation strategy

questiontext.text: All of the following are included in 'Ex-situ conservation' except

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Biodiversity conservation strategies are categorized into in-situ (on-site conservation within natural habitats) and ex-situ (off-site conservation outside natural habitats).

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, and seed banks involve taking endangered species or genetic material out of their natural habitats to protect them in specialized human-managed facilities (ex-situ conservation).
  • Sacred groves are tracts of natural forest protected on site through traditional culture and religious belief, representing in-situ conservation.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, sacred groves are excluded from ex-situ conservation.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_Q155 - Matching environmental phenomena with causative factors

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Environmental pollution and ecological phenomena have specific anthropogenic and ecological causes.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Eutrophication: Natural or artificial nutrient enrichment of water bodies (particularly nitrogen and phosphorus), leading to algal blooms.
  • Sanitary landfill: Method of solid waste disposal where wastes are dumped in trenches and covered with dirt daily.
  • Snow blindness: Inflammation of cornea caused by high doses of UV-B radiation reflected from snow.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q157 - Plant part used for smack extraction

questiontext.text: Which part of poppy plant is used to obtain the drug "Smack" ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Opioid drugs are plant derivatives or synthetic compounds that act on central nervous system opioid receptors.

Evaluation of Concepts: "Smack" (chemically diacetylmorphine) is a central nervous system depressant derived by acetylation of morphine. Morphine is extracted directly from the milky latex obtained by incising unripened capsules of the opium poppy plant (Papaver somniferum).

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the latex of the poppy plant is used to obtain the drug Smack.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q158 - Identification of non operon genetic element

questiontext.text: All of the following are part of an operon except

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: An operon is a coordinated genetic regulatory unit found in prokaryotes consisting of genes under the control of a single promoter and operator.

Evaluation of Concepts: A classical prokaryotic operon contains structural genes (coding for functional enzymes), a promoter (binding site for RNA polymerase), an operator (binding site for repressor protein), and a regulatory gene. Enhancers are eukaryotic gene regulatory DNA elements located far from the promoter, not components of prokaryotic operons.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, an enhancer is not part of an operon.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q159 - Inheritance pattern of maternal X linked condition

questiontext.text: A woman has an X-linked condition on one of her X chromosomes. This chromosome can be inherited by

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Transmission of sex-linked genes follows specific patterns based on sex chromosome inheritance from parents to offspring.

Evaluation of Concepts: A female individual has two X chromosomes (\(\text{XX}\)). During gametogenesis, she passes one of her X chromosomes to every offspring: daughters receive one X chromosome from the mother and one X from the father, while sons receive one X chromosome from the mother and a Y chromosome from the father. Thus, an X-linked trait on a mother's X chromosome can be transmitted to both sons and daughters.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the X chromosome carrying the condition can be inherited by both sons and daughters.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q160 - Mechanism of evolution proposed by De Vries

questiontext.text: According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Evolutionary theories propose different mechanisms for origin of species and speciation.

Evaluation of Concepts: Hugo de Vries based his Mutation Theory on experiments with evening primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana). He proposed that speciation occurs due to single-step large mutations, termed saltation, rather than the gradual minor variations proposed by Charles Darwin.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, according to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is saltation.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q161 - Transcription sequence of mRNA from coding DNA

questiontext.text: AGGTATCGCAT is a sequence from the coding strand of a gene. What will be the corresponding sequence of the transcribed mRNA ?

generalfeedback.text:
1. Given Data and Conditions:

  • Coding strand DNA sequence: \(\text{5'-AGGTATCGCAT-3'}\)

2. Relevant Principles: During transcription, RNA polymerase synthesizes mRNA complementary to the template DNA strand. The sequence of the transcribed mRNA is identical to the coding (non-template) strand of DNA in the \(\text{5'}\rightarrow\text{3'}\) direction, except that thymine (\(\text{T}\)) in DNA is replaced by uracil (\(\text{U}\)) in RNA.

3. Step-by-Step Working:

\[ \text{Coding Strand (DNA): } \text{5'-A G G T A T C G C A T-3'} \] \[ \text{Transcribed mRNA: } \text{5'-A G G U A U C G C A U-3'} \]

Replacing every \(\text{T}\) with \(\text{U}\) yields \(\text{AGGUAUCGCAU}\).

4. Final Answer: Therefore, the corresponding transcribed mRNA sequence is \(\text{AGGUAUCGCAU}\).

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_Q162 - Matching phases of human menstrual cycle

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column IColumn II
a.Proliferative Phasei.Breakdown of endometrial lining
b.Secretory Phaseii.Follicular Phase
c.Menstruationiii.Luteal Phase

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: The human menstrual cycle involves coordinated endocrine and physiological changes divided into menstrual, follicular/proliferative, and luteal/secretory phases.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Proliferative Phase: Also known as the follicular phase, during which primary follicles grow into mature Graafian follicles and the uterine endometrium regenerates.
  • Secretory Phase: Also known as the luteal phase, during which the corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain and prepare the endometrium for potential implantation.
  • Menstruation: Marked by the breakdown and shedding of the endometrial lining along with blood flow.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the correct matching links Proliferative Phase with Follicular Phase, Secretory Phase with Luteal Phase, and Menstruation with breakdown of endometrial lining.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_Q163 - Matching excretory system disorders with descriptions

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Pathological conditions of the human excretory system alter normal urine composition and renal structure.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Glycosuria: Excretion/presence of glucose in urine, commonly seen in diabetes mellitus.
  • Gout: Form of arthritis caused by accumulation and crystallization of uric acid in joints.
  • Renal calculi: Formation of insoluble mass of crystallized salts (such as oxalates) within the kidney.
  • Glomerular nephritis: Inflammatory condition of the glomeruli of kidneys.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the correct matching links Glycosuria with glucose in urine, Gout with uric acid in joints, Renal calculi with crystallized salt mass, and Glomerular nephritis with inflammation in glomeruli.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_Q164 - Matching nephron structures with excretory functions

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I (Function)Column II (Part of Excretory System)
a.Ultrafiltrationi.Henle's loop
b.Concentration of urineii.Ureter
c.Transport of urineiii.Urinary bladder
d.Storage of urineiv.Malpighian corpuscle
v.Proximal convoluted tubule

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Different anatomical subdivisions of the nephron and urinary tract execute specialized steps in excretion and osmoregulation.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Ultrafiltration: Occurs across the filtration membrane in the Malpighian corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman's capsule).
  • Concentration of urine: Achieved through counter-current multiplication in Henle's loop.
  • Transport of urine: Carried from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder via the ureter.
  • Storage of urine: Temporarily stored in the muscular urinary bladder prior to micturition.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, ultrafiltration occurs in Malpighian corpuscle, concentration of urine in Henle's loop, transport of urine via ureter, and storage of urine in urinary bladder.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q165 - Gastric cells indirectly assisting in erythropoiesis

questiontext.text: Which of the following gastric cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Erythropoiesis (red blood cell production) requires specific essential vitamins whose absorption depends on gastric mucosal secretions.

Evaluation of Concepts: Parietal cells (oxyntic cells) in the gastric mucosa secrete hydrochloric acid (\(\text{HCl}\)) and Castle's intrinsic factor. Intrinsic factor is essential for the intestinal absorption of vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) (cyanocobalamin) in the ileum. Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) is essential for erythroblast maturation during erythropoiesis. Thus, parietal cells indirectly support erythropoiesis.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, parietal cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_Q166 - Matching plasma proteins with physiological functions

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q167 - Identification of occupational respiratory lung disorder

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Occupational respiratory disorders arise from long-term inhalation of harmful dust particles or fibers in specific work environments.

Evaluation of Concepts: Silicosis is an occupational lung disease caused by chronic inhalation of silica dust in mining, stone-breaking, sandblasting, and construction industries, leading to pulmonary fibrosis and lung damage. Botulism is a foodborne bacterial toxin illness, Anthrax is an infectious disease caused by Bacillus anthracis, and Emphysema is predominantly caused by cigarette smoking.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q168 - Role of calcium ions in skeletal muscle contraction

generalfeedback.text:

This binding induces a conformational change in troponin, shifting tropomyosin away to unmask the active myosin-binding sites on the actin filaments, allowing cross-bridge formation between actin and myosin.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, calcium binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q169 - Composition of Nissl bodies in neurons

questiontext.text: Nissl bodies are mainly composed of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Nissl bodies (Nissl granules) are large granular basophilic structures found in the soma and dendrites of neurons.

Evaluation of Concepts: Nissl bodies consist of dense aggregations of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) studded with membrane-bound ribosomes along with free ribosomes. They actively synthesize proteins needed for neuronal metabolism, neurotransmitter precursor production, and cell maintenance.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, Nissl bodies are mainly composed of free ribosomes and RER.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q170 - Evaluation of cellular respiration statements

questiontext.text: Which of these statements is incorrect ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Cellular respiration involves compartmentalized metabolic pathways across different regions of the cell and mitochondrion.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol and requires a supply of \(\text{NAD}^+\) to accept electrons/hydrogens during the oxidation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.
  • TCA cycle (Krebs cycle) enzymes are located soluble in the mitochondrial matrix (except succinate dehydrogenase on the inner membrane).
  • Oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport system (ETS) occur on the inner mitochondrial membrane (cristae), not on the outer mitochondrial membrane.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, stating that oxidative phosphorylation takes place in the outer mitochondrial membrane is incorrect.

Conceptual Principle: Distinct chromosome structural forms and specialized giant chromosome types perform specific cellular roles.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Allosomes are sex chromosomes that determine sex.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q172 - Descriptive terms for human dentition

questiontext.text: Which of the following terms describe human dentition ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Human dental anatomy is characterized by structural attachment, developmental frequency, and morphological differentiation.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Thecodont: Teeth are embedded in deep sockets of jawbones (maxilla and mandible).
  • Diphyodont: Teeth develop in two successive sets during life: a deciduous/milk set replaced by a permanent set.
  • Heterodont: Teeth are differentiated into morphologically distinct types (incisors, canines, premolars, molars).

Final Conclusion: Therefore, human dentition is described as thecodont, diphyodont, and heterodont.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q173 - Processes occurring in rough endoplasmic reticulum

questiontext.text: Which of the following events does not occur in rough endoplasmic reticulum ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Endoplasmic reticulum sub-domains specialize in distinct biosynthetic and processing pathways.

Evaluation of Concepts: The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER), studded with ribosomes, is specialized for protein synthesis, signal peptide cleavage, protein folding (assisted by chaperones), and core protein glycosylation. Phospholipid and lipid biosynthesis takes place in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER).

Final Conclusion: Therefore, phospholipid synthesis does not occur in the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q174 - Structure formed by multiple ribosomes on mRNA

questiontext.text: Many ribosomes may associate with a single mRNA to form multiple copies of a polypeptide simultaneously. Such strings of ribosomes are termed as

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: During protein translation, multiple ribosomes simultaneously translate a single mRNA molecule to increase translation efficiency.

Evaluation of Concepts: A linear sequence of multiple ribosomes actively translating a single strand of mRNA is termed a polysome or polyribosome. This structure enables rapid, simultaneous production of multiple polypeptide copies from a single mRNA template.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, strings of ribosomes associated with a single mRNA are termed polysomes.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q175 - Disease causing chronic lymphatic inflammation

questiontext.text: In which disease does mosquito transmitted pathogen cause chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Vector-borne parasitic diseases affect specific target tissues, leading to characteristic clinical pathology.

Evaluation of Concepts: Elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis) is caused by the filarial nematode worms Wuchereria bancrofti and Wuchereria malayi, transmitted by the bite of female Culex mosquitoes. The adult worms reside in lymphatic vessels, triggering chronic inflammation, blockage, and severe swelling of lower limbs and genitalia.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the disease characterized by chronic lymphatic inflammation caused by a mosquito-transmitted pathogen is elephantiasis.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q176 - Identification of non autoimmune disease

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not an autoimmune disease ?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system loses self-tolerance and mistakenly attacks healthy bodily tissues.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Rheumatoid arthritis (immune attack on synovial joint membranes), psoriasis (immune-mediated rapid skin cell turnover), and vitiligo (autoimmune destruction of melanocytes) are recognized autoimmune disorders.
  • Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by extracellular beta-amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tau tangles, not classified as an autoimmune disease.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, Alzheimer's disease is not an autoimmune disease.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q177 - Identification of non divergent evolution example

questiontext.text: Among the following sets of examples for divergent evolution, select the incorrect option :

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Evolutionary relationships are reflected in anatomical structures resulting from common ancestry (divergent evolution/homology) or adaptation to similar environments (convergent evolution/analogy).

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Forelimbs, brains, and hearts of mammals (man, bat, cheetah) are homologous structures derived from common ancestral lineages via divergent evolution.
  • The eye of an octopus (mollusk) and the eye of mammals (bat, man) perform similar photoreceptive visual functions but have completely different embryonic origins and developmental pathways, representing convergent evolution.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, the eye of octopus, bat, and man represents convergent evolution, making it an incorrect example of divergent evolution.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q178 - Nutritional enrichment in milk curd conversion

questiontext.text: Conversion of milk to curd improves its nutritional value by increasing the amount of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Fermentation of dairy products by beneficial microflora enhances nutritional quality and digestibility.

Evaluation of Concepts: During curd formation from milk, lactic acid bacteria (LAB) such as Lactobacillus ferment lactose into lactic acid, coagulating milk proteins and significantly boosting the content of Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\).

Final Conclusion: Therefore, conversion of milk to curd increases the amount of Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\).

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q179 - Vertebrate forelimb bone similarity as homology

questiontext.text: The similarity of bone structure in the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Homologous organs possess similar anatomical designs and embryonic developmental origins due to shared ancestry, even though they may perform different functions.

Evaluation of Concepts: The forelimbs of humans, bats, cheetahs, and whales share a common structural pattern of bones (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges), indicating divergent evolution from a common ancestral vertebrate. This anatomical structural similarity is termed homology.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, similarity of forelimb bone structure in vertebrates is an example of homology.

name.text: NEET_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q180 - Characteristics of human blood group inheritance

questiontext.text:
Which of the following characteristics represent 'Inheritance of blood groups' in humans ?

a. Dominance
b. Co-dominance
c. Multiple allele
d. Incomplete dominance
e. Polygenic inheritance

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle: Human ABO blood group inheritance is governed by the \(I\) gene, displaying multiple genetic inheritance principles.

Evaluation of Concepts:

  • Dominance: Alleles \(I^A\) and \(I^B\) are completely dominant over allele \(i\).
  • Co-dominance: When alleles \(I^A\) and \(I^B\) are both present (\(I^A I^B\)), both red blood cell surface antigens A and B are expressed simultaneously.
  • Multiple allelism: Three alleles (\(I^A\), \(I^B\), and \(i\)) exist in the human population for the single \(I\) gene locus.

Final Conclusion: Therefore, inheritance of human blood groups represents dominance, co-dominance, and multiple alleles.
